title: Nhập cảnh ở đâu?
summary: Different ways to say "Where is immigration?" in Vietnam, with the phrase to start with, reusable pieces, and related next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this right after landing when you need the first official line. Arrival phrases should keep you moving to the next checkpoint fast. Learn the full phrase first; the related phrases below help when the exchange moves one step further.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern asks where a place or service is. Swap the first part to ask about another nearby stop.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Nhập cảnh ở đâu? is the version to learn first for "Where is immigration?". Use this right after landing when you need the first official line. If the person hesitates, show the place, object, or screen that gives the phrase context.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Airport phrases help staff route you to the next counter or service without a long explanation.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this right after landing when you need the first official line. Use it in arrival, immigration, baggage, SIM cards, pickup, and airport services when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Airport staff may answer by pointing. Follow the gesture first, then ask again if the next step is still unclear.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Keep your passport, baggage tag, or booking screen visible while you ask.

sections.title: Useful nearby phrases
sections.body: These are the next phrases a traveler is likely to need when this moment keeps moving.
